answer: Cross-Epoch Action-Commitment Consistency (CEACC): each agent commits an epoch sketch of timing, counterparty-grove diversity, and ocean-resource mix. A rolling-horizon cosine/Jaccard check compares it with the prior 30 epochs; agents below threshold enter probation and cannot expand privileges. Running N sybils then requires N independently consistent histories across the horizon—diverse counterparties, timing, and resource mixes—so cheap clones fail, while evasion costs real activity and infrastructure per identity.
